bullets.title: META Muse: AMZN blocks AI shopping agent citing unauthorized access; app hits #1
bullets.body: Amazon cut off Meta's Muse personal AI agent from shopping on Amazon.com, citing ToS violations including failure to identify itself, unauthorized site access, web scraping, and capture of customer credentials. Despite the block, META Muse hit #1 in the iOS App Store with strong mainstream pickup; available on Mac with file/message/calendar access. Wells Fargo separately raised META PT to $796 from $640, maintaining Overweight.

bullets.title: MRVL: Morgan Stanley raises PT to $268; announces industry-first 2nm optical interconnect
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley raised Marvell Technology's price target to $268 from $246. Separately, Marvell announced industry-first 2nm optical interconnect demonstrations targeting next-generation AI data center connectivity — bullish read-through for MRVL's AI infrastructure positioning.

bullets.title: ARM +14%, AMD +9% on heavy unusual volume; SOX at multi-year P/E discount
bullets.body: ARM traded at 156% of 30-day average volume (+14.2% to $314.79) and AMD hit a new 52-week high at $611 (+9.2%), trading at 112% of normal volume, both attributed to sector momentum and Meta Muse read-throughs. The SOX index hit a 20% discount to the S&P at 13.6x forward P/E vs. its 5-year median of 20.5x; Morgan Stanley remains constructive on quality/AI adopters within semis.

bullets.title: NVDA: Power shortfall rises to 57GW by 2028; Rubin rack power surges to 234kW
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley estimates the US data center power shortfall through 2028 rises to 57GW gross (33GW net), up from prior 38GW estimate, with another 68GW of incremental demand in 2029. NVDA's Vera Rubin rack power consumption revised to 234kW (vs. 149kW prior), Rubin Ultra to 600kW (vs. 415kW). Cost/TFLOP falls 94% from Hopper to Rubin Ultra, triggering Jevons paradox and higher aggregate electricity demand. Separately, Jensen Huang projects chip sales to double next year following 70% FY28 revenue growth guidance.

bullets.title: CRWD PT raised to $254, PANW to $410 at Morgan Stanley; cybersecurity AI spend could hit 4%
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley raises CrowdStrike to OW with PT $254 (from $238), citing AIDR nearly tripling Q/Q, EDR accelerating for the 4th consecutive quarter, and NNARR +51% y/y. Palo Alto raised to OW Top Pick at PT $410 (from $394) with XSIAM ARR >$700M +70% y/y and Prisma AIRS at ~$120M ARR. AI safety scrutiny is seen as increasing compute/capex requirements, not derailing the infrastructure cycle; cybersecurity currently ~1.5% of enterprise AI spend with a bull case of 4% by 2028.

bullets.title: TSLA: Oppenheimer site visit — Cybercab real, Optimus delayed to late 2027/early 2028
bullets.body: Oppenheimer's TSLA site visit concludes autonomy is "increasingly real": Cybercab uses 5 parallel module production enabling 40% material cost reduction, and production estimates are doubled to ~3k vehicles/quarter in late 2028. However, Optimus commercial deployment pushed back two quarters to late 2027/early 2028, and energy storage growth rate cut from 25% to 20% due to de-emphasis and competitive crosswinds. Stock described as in "no man's land" with key value drivers still years away.

bullets.title: CRM: Salesforce showing record Dreamforce pipeline; 60-80% pricing uplift on premium upgrades
bullets.body: Truist's Dreamforce channel checks show record pipeline with high-teen growth and healthier coverage ratios. Premium AI upgrades are generating 60-80% pricing uplift and 1.4x ARR expansion at the account level. JPMorgan is hosting a software sector update call on Sept 23 to discuss Dreamforce and HubSpot UNBOUND partner feedback.

bullets.title: AAPL: iPhone 18 Pro/Max lead times weakening, especially China; Hedgeye maintains short
bullets.body: Hedgeye reports Week 2 iPhone 18 Pro/Pro Max lead times are weak: China Pro fell to 11 days from 30 days YoY and China Pro Max to 15 days from 37 days YoY. US lead times are marginally below year-ago. US carrier promotions ($100 more aggressive vs. iPhone 17) are partially cushioning demand but Hedgeye maintains its short thesis. iFixit also notes Apple's new variable aperture lens is a feat of engineering but effectively unrepairable.

bullets.title: WBD +9.9% on Paramount-Skydance antitrust settlement; options volume 442% above normal
bullets.body: Warner Bros. Discovery surged 9.9% to $30.54 after Paramount Skydance reached a settlement in California's antitrust case. Key terms: $1.5B California production investment, commitment to release 30 films/year (or pay $30M per shortfall), and potential separate initial operations of WBD and Paramount studios. WBD options volume hit 356,832 contracts vs. 80,675 average — 442% above normal.

bullets.title: MSFT: Dividend raised 7.7% to $0.98/qtr; AI capex front-loaded, enterprise RPO inflecting
bullets.body: Microsoft increased its quarterly dividend 7.7% to $0.98 (from $0.91, effective Sept 15). Goldman Sachs notes all of Q4's $51B RPO increase came from enterprise customers (not frontier labs), validating MSFT's AI strategy. Forward P/E has rebounded off lows but remains below its 10-year average vs. the S&P, with NY's new RAISE Act (effective Jan 2027) requiring large AI developers to publish safety frameworks and report critical incidents within 72 hours.

bullets.title: APP: eCommerce store growth fastest in 5 months; gross ad spend ~$20B vs $11B in Jan 2025
bullets.body: Citi maintains Buy on AppLovin: global eCommerce clients reached 13,105 as of Sept 18, up 5.1% w/w — the fastest weekly growth in five months — driven by China (+72.5%) and Hong Kong (+17.3%). Gross ad spend has grown ~82% since January 2025 disclosure, from $11B to ~$20B today. US store concentration fell to 57.2% as international mix expands.

bullets.title: RBLX: Citi maintains Buy; QTD bookings tracking $1.67B, above guidance and consensus
bullets.body: Citi's RoMonitor data shows Week 38 average peak CCUs at 15.9M (down 15% YoY but stabilized by new hit 'Steal an Egg'). QTD data implies bookings of $1.67B, above company guidance of $1.65B and Visible Alpha consensus of $1.61B. JPMorgan's gaming survey notes ~54% of US Roblox users have reduced spend, with algo optimizations (RFY) expected to improve LTV/monetization.

bullets.title: INTC: SK Hynix exploring Ohio fab partnership; substrate capacity concern raised
bullets.body: The memory market rundown notes SK Hynix is exploring a partnership with Intel to build US memory-chip capacity, potentially leasing Intel's Ohio fab or forming a joint venture. Separately, an industry observer flagged concern that Intel may not have secured adequate substrate capacity to meet customer demand, including for a large Qualcomm CPU (codenamed Rolex) requiring EMIB-T advanced packaging.

bullets.title: MU: Taiwan union threatens strike; demonstrates first 512GB DDR5 module; memory spot prices rising
bullets.body: Micron's Taiwan union threatened a strike over profit-sharing at a key DRAM/HBM plant. Micron also demonstrated the world's first 512GB DDR5 module, targeting volume production in H2'27. Memory spot prices are tightening sharply: DDR5 +5.3% M/M and DRAM modules +23.1% M/M. Samsung plans to at least double HBM4 production in 2027 amid persistent market tightness.

bullets.title: HPE upgraded to OW at Morgan Stanley; CIOs pulling forward server/storage spend
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley upgrades HPE to Overweight citing chipflation tailwinds and AI infrastructure demand pulling forward 2027 capacity. 70-75% of CIOs are pulling forward 2026 PC, storage, and server spending, and 20-30% are also pulling forward 2027. ~60% of enterprises expect incremental on-prem compute/storage needs for AI, but 70%+ of AI inferencing is still expected in the public cloud.

bullets.title: T upgraded to Outperform at BNP Paribas Exane; PT raised to $30 from $26
bullets.body: BNP Paribas Exane upgrades AT&T to Outperform from Neutral and raises its price target to $30 from $26, citing fiber-led convergence strategy with compelling long-term returns and near-term wireless tailwinds. The firm also expects a muted iPhone upgrade cycle in Q3 to benefit carrier margins.

bullets.title: CIEN: Evercore ISI upgrades to Outperform, raises PT to $550 from $375
bullets.body: Ciena was upgraded to Outperform from In-Line at Evercore ISI with a price target raised to $550 from $375, reflected in a +6.4% pre-market move. The upgrade comes amid broader optical networking strength as hedge funds increase exposure to the sector.

bullets.title: DLR/EQIX: Redburn initiates both at Buy; data center supply blocked by community opposition
bullets.body: Redburn initiates Digital Realty at Buy with a $227 PT and Equinix at Buy with a $1,261 PT. The backdrop remains constructive: Q2 saw 45 US data center projects delayed/blocked totaling ~$68B due to community opposition, while hyperscalers have accumulated ~$300B in off-balance-sheet AI guarantees over the trailing twelve months.

bullets.title: TXN: Dividend raised 7.0% to $1.52/qtr
bullets.body: Texas Instruments increased its quarterly dividend 7.0% to $1.52 from $1.42, effective September 17. No rating or PT changes noted in the digest window.

bullets.title: RH: Estates gallery launches, embeds ~8pts to 4Q revenue guide; targets 50% of offering in 5 years
bullets.body: Hedgeye notes RH Estates opened its first full RH Ecosystem location in Greenwich (Estates + Outdoor + Gallery + hospitality), with a Melrose location planned for 2027. The Estates segment is embedded in RH's ~8pt contribution to the 4Q revenue guide, with management targeting Estates representing 50% of total RH offering within five years. Furniture promotional intensity has also eased after a summer discount peak in July.
